title: Performance Sleuth: Canary vs Prod Diff Notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on, incremental notebook for chasing down small-but-real performance regressions surfaced by our canary stack. The goal is to have an actionable, repeatable checklist that any oncall or engineer can follow when a canary P95/P99 delta or tokens/sec degradation appears versus prod.

Context / recent signal:
- Canary job: canary-us-west-2-v2 (traffic ~2%).
- Alert: canary.p95_latency > prod.p95_latency + 18ms for model-id: opt-7b-q8.
- Observed across 4 consecutive canary runs over 48h, correlated with mild GPU scheduler stalls on host g4-045.
- Ticket: JIRA-RT-4123 (owner: Priya Kaur).

High-level hypotheses (start wide, narrow quickly):
1) Workload shift: longer average sequence lengths in canary dataset (prompt sampling) -> more KV cache pressure.
2) Kernel selection mismatch: runtime selected slower matmul kernel on canary due to environment var / compiler change.
3) Contention: background maintenance job (checkpoint upload / snapshot) interfering with device PCIe or NVMe bandwidth.
4) Memory allocator fragmentation / OOM leading to heavier GC/allocs on CPU side.
5) Version drift: a new runtime binary landed in canary that changed batching behavior or tokenization preprocessing.

Priority checklist (90-minute triage window):
- [ ] Verify the alert characteristics: time windows, affected routes, model versions (promQL/Datadog queries appended).
- [ ] Reproduce the delta using stored canary traffic in replay mode (replay-run --target canary-us-west-2-v2 --window 2026-03-08T02:00Z).
- [ ] Collect short traces: per-request trace with KV cache hit/miss, kernel labels, and device-side timestamps.
- [ ] Capture system profiles during the anomalous run: perf, nvprof/ncu, and pprof CPU/heap on runtime process.
- [ ] Bisect config diff between canary and prod (image tag, env vars, kernel libs).
- [ ] If immediate mitigation needed: rollback canary to previous image or enable fallback model variant for affected route.

Quick reproduction commands (use the canary replay infra):
- rwi canary replay --id canary-us-west-2-v2 --start 2026-03-08T02:00:00Z --duration 00:30:00 --capture-trace=/tmp/canary-run-0308.trace
- # start system profiler on host (root)
- sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 1800 &
- # capture runtime pprof endpoint (if enabled)
- curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=60 > /tmp/pprof_cpu.pb
- go tool pprof -http=:8081 /usr/bin/serving-runtime /tmp/pprof_cpu.pb  # interactive flamegraph

Important signals to compare (canary vs prod):
- Request-level: p50/p95/p99 latency (server and device breakdown), queue wait time, preprocessing time, decode time per token, tokens/sec.
- Device-level: GPU utilization, SM occupancy, tensor core utilization, memory alloc/reclaim counts, PCIe transfer size/time.
- Host-level: steal time, runqueue length, nvme IO wait, process context-switches, malloc fragmentation.
- Runtime-level: batching distribution (batch sizes over time), KV cache hit rate, kernel name frequency, compilation fallback events.

PromQL / Datadog queries (examples):
- p95 latency delta: 100 * (quantile(0.95, rate(request_latency_ms{env=\"canary\"}[5m])) - quantile(0.95, rate(request_latency_ms{env=\"prod\"}[5m]))) / quantile(0.95, rate(request_latency_ms{env=\"prod\"}[5m]))
- batching histogram: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(serving_batch_size_bucket[1m])) by (le, model))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups[5m])) by (model)

Profiling cookbook (what to capture and why):
- perf (system-wide): identifies kernel/IO stalls, syscalls, context-switch hotspots. Use with -g for callgraph.
- nvprof / ncu: captures GPU kernel timelines, launch latency, memcpy times. Look for long memcpy (host->device) spikes overlapping with tails.
- pprof (Go/C++ runtime): CPU flamegraphs for runtime threads, GC pause metrics (if applicable), and allocation hotspots.
- trace-level: distributed trace capturing timestamps at: request received, preproc end, batch enter, kernel start, kernel end, decode end, response sent. Add request-scoped GPU timestamps via NVTX to correlate.

Bisect plan (config + code + infra):
1) Compare container images: docker inspect on canary vs prod -> diff binary checksums for /usr/bin/serving-runtime and linked lib versions (libtorch, cuda).
2) Environment: diff /etc/ld.so.conf.d, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, LD_PRELOAD values.
3) Feature flags: flip any new runtime flags (e.g., CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=true/false) in a controlled canary toggling experiment.
4) Kernel sources: if a new kernel selection landed, run microbenchmarks (matmul/query) with both kernels to quantify difference.

If you suspect batching/queueing:
- Run synthetic load generating 1-1.2x normal qps with fixed short/long prompts and measure batch-size distribution.
- Use rwi trace-ui to show per-batcher latency percentiles; look for increased variance in batch formation time.

Decision tree for root cause after profiles (example):
- If perf shows heavy syscalls / NVMe IO overlapping with tails -> investigate snapshot/upload jobs (check cron jobs and backup processes on host), consider moving uploads to lower-priority cgroup.
- If nvprof shows increased memcpy H2D time -> check PCIe traffic and co-running processes; consider live-migration to different host or draining.
- If pprof shows hotspots in tokenization or CPU preproc -> roll back tokenization library version, or deploy a fastpath pre-tokenized dataset for canary.
- If kernel selection different and slow -> pin kernel selector flag to previous commit and run microbench before promoting change.

Mitigation playbook (fast):
1) Rollback canary image to previous stable tag (rwi deploy --canary --image redwood/runtime:2026-01-04-stable).
2) Disable continuous_batched_encoder flag which changes batch windowing.
3) Re-route traffic to dedicated slower-but-stable model variant (opt-7b-q4f32-fallback) for affected route.
4) If host-level contention suspected: cordon host, live-migrate canary pods, and mark host for deeper host-level forensic.

Artifacts to gather and attach to ticket JIRA-RT-4123:
- /tmp/perf.data, /tmp/pprof_cpu.pb, /tmp/canary-run-0308.trace, nvprof log (/tmp/ncu-report.txt), batcher histogram csv, and a short summary (1-paragraph) with conclusion and recommended rollback.

Notes / gotchas from prior hunts:
- Small env var changes (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 vs unset) flipped allocator behavior and caused 12–18ms p95 deltas. Always diff env vars.
- GPU kernel fallback can be non-deterministic; reproduce with pinned seeds and identical CPU load.
- Canary traffic distribution can differ in prompt length; always normalize by median tokens/request when comparing tokens/sec.

Next steps / owners:
- Priya Kaur: run replay + trace capture and attach artifacts (due 2026-03-11).
- Marco Alvarez: run microbench kernel comparisons and report matrix of kernels x sequence_length (due 2026-03-12).
- Aisha Raman (owner): own ticket, coordinate rollback if needed and write postmortem template.

Scratch log (raw findings):
- 2026-03-09 03:12: canary run spike, perf shows host read IO at 34ms blocking on /dev/nvme0n1.
- 2026-03-09 03:18: nvprof shows memcpy H2D spikes at 12–15ms for some requests, correlates with larger-than-usual batch sizes.
- 2026-03-10 13:04: discovered cron job snapshot-uploader running at 03:00 UTC on canary nodes only (misconfigured cron on canary AMI). Hypothesis: overlapping NVMe uploads causing IO pressure and memcpy slowdown.

If cron uploader confirmed: schedule immediate mitigation -> move uploader to low io nice (ionice -c3) + stagger windows across nodes; longer-term: throttle uploads or use async off-host snapshots.

End of notebook. Paste artifacts into JIRA-RT-4123 and ping #eng-serving-runtime with summary once rollback or fix is in place.
